description:
Why this choice is correct: AiaError at pkix-aia/src/lib.rs:111-205 is marked #[non_exhaustive] and uses struct variant shape (e.g. ResponseTooLarge { limit, actual }) rather than tuple variant shape (ResponseTooLarge(usize, usize)) for any variant carrying more than one field.

#[non_exhaustive] is the right call for a public error enum on a pre-1.0 crate that will expand over time. Future variants for DNS resolution, TLS validation of the AIA endpoint, etc. (already foreseen in the rustdoc at lines 81-83) can land without breaking downstream pattern matches.

Struct variants for ResponseTooLarge and IoFailure are right because:
- Pattern matchers read better: 'AiaError::ResponseTooLarge { limit, actual }' is self-documenting; 'AiaError::ResponseTooLarge(a, b)' requires checking which is which.
- Field reordering is non-breaking (struct variants are matched by name).
- Future field additions (e.g. timing data, request ID) can land without breaking existing matches that use '..' rest pattern.

A future contributor might suggest 'tuple variants are more concise — use ResponseTooLarge(usize, usize)'. Reject: the readability and future-proofing of struct shape are worth the extra punctuation.
title: Decision: #[non_exhaustive] AiaError with struct variants for multi-field cases
